Strategy: Separator pressure is governed by the balance between vapor recycled/removed via the compressor loop. The compressor recycle valve (xmv_5) is an anti-surge/bypass valve: opening it diverts flow away from the compressor suction, reducing the net vapor actually pulled out of the separator overhead, so it should act as a "reduced outflow" term with a POSITIVE effect on Δpressure. Compressor work (xmeas_20) is a direct proxy for how much vapor is actually being compressed/removed from the separator vapor space — higher compressor work means more gas extraction, i.e., higher outflow, giving a NEGATIVE effect on Δpressure. I deliberately excluded the composition variables (xmeas_25/31/33/35/38) from this generation because they are chromatograph-sampled (piecewise-constant between analyzer cycles) and would only be justifiable under the Dalton's-law category, which I am not invoking here to keep this a clean single-law test. I also avoided any reactor/stripper state variables per the cross-unit trap rule, and did not include xmeas_13 lag since it is explicitly disallowed as an input. If the sign check fails (e.g., xmv_5 shows negative due to controller confounding — since xmv_5 itself may be a controller output responding to compressor surge conditions correlated with pressure), I will switch to the Valve/orifice flow characteristic law and introduce a sqrt/nonlinear valve function, or consider Dalton's partial pressure law using xmeas_31/33/35 (purge composition) scaled by a total flow/pressure reference term.

Strategy: The validated Law-1 (mass balance, F_in − F_out) triad from Gen 7/9 — xmeas_6 as inflow, xmeas_20 and xmeas_10 as outflow proxies — remains the best sign-check-passing structure so far. Every attempt to add xmv_5 as a *standalone* linear outflow term (Gens 1–2) failed sign check, which I attributed to closed-loop anti-surge-controller confounding: xmv_5's raw position correlates with pressure through the controller's own response pattern, not through an open-loop physical channel, so a bare linear coefficient on xmv_5 picks up the wrong (controller-driven) sign.

This generation reintroduces xmv_5, but not as an independent additive term — instead as a *physically motivated multiplicative modulator* of the already-validated xmeas_20 (compressor work) outflow term. The physical mechanism: xmeas_20 represents total compressor throughput/work extracting vapor from the separator overhead, but a fraction of that circulated gas is diverted back through the anti-surge/recycle bypass (xmv_5) rather than actually leaving the separator's mass-balance boundary net of recycle. So the *effective* net vapor extraction rate is better represented as xmeas_20*(1 − xmv_5/100): when xmv_5 is fully open (100), the effective outflow this term contributes goes to zero (all recycled internally, no net removal); when xmv_5 is closed (0), the full xmeas_20 outflow proxy applies. This is a bona fide instance of the mass-balance F_out term, refined by a physically grounded gating factor, not a new law category or an added correlation-chasing term — the underlying claim (higher effective compressor extraction ⇒ more negative Δpressure) is unchanged from the already-validated Gen 6/7/9 result, only the "effective outflow magnitude" is now more accurately computed.

Expected signs: c[1] positive (xmeas_6 inflow, validated in Gens 7/9/11/12), c[2] positive (since the term already carries an explicit leading minus sign, a positive c[2] means the effective-outflow product term reduces Δpressure, consistent with prior xmeas_20 outflow sign), c[3] negative-consistent i.e. positive coefficient on the explicit minus (xmeas_10 outflow, validated across Gens 6,7,9,11,12), c[4] unconstrained intercept.

If c[2] fails sign check, this will be strong evidence that xmv_5's controller confounding is not resolved even by this multiplicative reframing, and I will drop xmv_5 entirely from future generations and revert to the clean, thrice-validated 3-term Gen 7/9 model as the final Law-1 answer, treating xmv_5 as unusable in any functional form for this target.

This generation keeps the validated 3-term outflow/inflow core completely unchanged (same variables, same expected signs) and adds one new, previously-untested, genuinely independent mass-flux term: xmeas_19 (Stripper Steam Flow). This is a literal flow-rate variable, not an accumulation-state variable of the stripper (it is not xmeas_15/16/18), so it does not violate the cross-unit accumulation-state trap. Physically, stripper steam strips light/volatile components out of the stripper bottoms liquid; the resulting overhead vapor from the stripper is routed back into the condenser/separator/compressor recycle loop.
